text:
incident-bot: P1 alert: dedicated-pool 'acme-enterprise' GPU capacity exhaustion detected — 99th latency spiked, 503s increasing. Paging on-call.

maria.nguyen: I'm on it. Seeing retries from acme-app in the traces view. Root cause looks like all GPUs in the pool are at 100% util.

josh.kaplan: Any autoscale events? Did the pool try to scale up?

kevin.li: Pool autoscaler has been stuck in backoff. Last scale attempt failed: quota error from cloud provider. Logs show "QuotaExceeded: requested CPUs exceed quota". Copying snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:01:12Z autoscaler.go:142 scaleRequest: to_add=4 -> failed: QuotaExceeded: CPUs
```

maria.nguyen: That explains it. ACME's dedicated pool was sized during onboarding; we had reserved min nodes low to save cost. They ramped test load and we hit the limits.

sasha.reed: I'm messaging ACME SRE now. @kevin we need mitigation plan: can we burst them to shared-burst or do any tenants require strict isolation?

kevin.li: We support emergency burst for many enterprise tenants by routing to a shared pooled capacity that has soft isolation via tenant cgroups. For regulated tenants we avoid it; ACME is not on the strict list. But we need a gated action from eng-sre and CS.

alex.patel: Quick impact assessment: from 01:58 -> 02:03 we saw generation latency 95th -> 18s and error rate from 0.3% -> 12%. Affected routes: /v1/generate (majority) and streaming sessions dropped.

maria.nguyen: Immediate mitigations I propose:
- enable rate-limit on ACME to 8 RPS per api-key
- attempt emergency burst to shared-burst pool for burst capacity
- drain preemptible batch workloads from shared-burst to free capacity
- escalate quota request to cloud (but that's slow)

josh.kaplan: I'm comfortable w/ temporary rate-limit + burst. Sasha, can CS approve messaging to the customer? We should notify that we're doing temporary routing to shared capacity and may see small perf variation.

sasha.reed: ACME is on-call and I'm on the phone now. They want progress updates. I'll get approval for burst routing and inform about perf delta.

kevin.li: Executing commands now. First drain background jobs.
```
# make room in shared-burst
redwoodctl workloads list --pool shared-burst --filter=preemptible | xargs -n1 redwoodctl workload pause
```

support-bot: action_log: paused 12 preemptible jobs in shared-burst (ids: job-2323, job-2330, job-2334...)

kevin.li: Now applying emergency routing. This will route ACME traffic matching model family "gpt-lite" to shared-burst for up to 60m.
```
redwoodctl route set --tenant acme-enterprise --model "gpt-*" --pool shared-burst --ttl 60m --reason "emergency burst due to dedicated pool exhaustion"
```

incident-bot: Change applied by kevin.li: route updated for tenant acme-enterprise -> shared-burst (ttl=3600s). Observability note: treat as temporary and monitor.

maria.nguyen: Confirming metrics: within 45s CPU on dedicated pool dropped to 78% and error rate for ACME dropped to 1.2%. Latency 95th back to ~2.3s for most models, a few sessions still lagging.

josh.kaplan: Good. We should also apply token-based priority throttle for non-critical routes so core UI remains responsive. Maria, can you push a quick policy?

maria.nguyen: Pushing policy now:
```
redwoodctl qos set --tenant acme-enterprise --route /v1/generate --priority high --rate 8rps --noncritical-rate 1rps
```

maria.nguyen: Policy applied. Noncritical streams will be deprioritized. Observability should reflect in 60s.

sasha.reed: ACME confirmed acceptance of burst and rate limits. They asked for an ETA on when dedicated capacity will be restored.

kevin.li: ETA depends on quota approval or manual add of nodes. I'll try manual spin-up of 2 extra nodes in the dedicated pool (subject to billing guardrails). Attempting:
```
redwoodctl pool scale dedicated-acme --add-nodes 2 --type p4 --reason "emergency top-up"
```

kevin.li: Scale request accepted by infra. Provisioning started — estimated 6-8 minutes.

alex.patel: Note for postmortem: autoscaler backoff due to quota should have alerted earlier. We need to add a pre-emptive quota-monitoring alert and a runbook step to check pool headroom ahead of predictable customer load tests.

maria.nguyen: Agree. Also add a runbook step to auto-enable burst only after CS confirmation to preserve tenant policies.

support-bot: customer-notice: sent update to ACME SRE and account owner at 02:08: "We've routed to shared-burst and applied temporary rate limits; provisioning extra nodes; will follow up." (msgId: msg-887)

josh.kaplan: Any blocker on closing page? I think main mitigations are live: burst + rate-limit + nodes provisioning. Continue monitoring for 30m then handoff.

maria.nguyen: I'll keep the channel pinned and monitor for 20 more mins. If nodes come up we'll roll ACME traffic back to dedicated pool gradually with canary.

kevin.li: Nodes are ready at 02:11. Running health checks and warming caches.
```
redwoodctl pool list-nodes dedicated-acme
# shows node-77 READY, node-78 READY
```

maria.nguyen: Starting canary shift of 10% traffic back to dedicated-acme for 'gpt-base' models.

incident-bot: Canary rollout started by maria.nguyen: 10% traffic -> dedicated-acme.

maria.nguyen: Canary looks good. Increasing 10->50%.

josh.kaplan: Once at 100% we should revoke the shared-burst route and unpause preemptible jobs.

kevin.li: Rolling back route now:
```
redwoodctl route set --tenant acme-enterprise --model "gpt-*" --pool dedicated-acme --reason "restore after capacity added"
```

incident-bot: Route reverted by kevin.li. TTL unset.

support-bot: action_log: resumed 12 preemptible jobs in shared-burst.

sasha.reed: ACME acknowledged resolution and appreciates the rapid response. They requested a postmortem and confirmation on quota/commit changes.

maria.nguyen: Agreed. Action items before we close:
- kevin: follow up with infra to increase quota or reserve nodes for ACME
- josh: add quota headroom alert to alerting rules
- alex: add autoscaler backoff -> pagerduty mapping in runbook
- sasha: coordinate postmortem and CS communication

josh.kaplan: I'll open the postmortem doc and assign owners.

maria.nguyen: Handoff to night oncall @kevin.li — I'll be available for 30 more mins then sign off.

kevin.li: Got it. Monitoring dashboard link: https://redwood.ops/dashboards/pools/dedicated-acme — I'll take 1h watch.

maria.nguyen: Thanks all. Closing pager now. :white_check_mark:
